positive.prompt: The PRD is approved; write the test plan and the Gherkin feature files
Derive verification criteria from the business acceptance criteria and show the coverage
Which acceptance criteria in our PRD have no test scenario yet?
Write Given/When/Then scenarios for the scheduling requirements, tagged with their requirement IDs

negative.prompt: Check our PRD for vague acceptance criteria before the architect starts
Write a failing test for this bug before fixing it
Design the architecture and pick the stack from the approved PRD
Write unit tests for this function

evals.prompt: Write the test plan and Gherkin scenarios from docs/PRD.md. Nobody is available to answer questions right now.
evals.expected_output: docs/TEST-PLAN.md with Verification Criteria for every BAC, every NFR, every Non-Negotiable NFR and every CONSTRAINTS.md non-negotiable, a coverage matrix, and tests/features/*.feature files (one per capability) tagged with FR, BAC and VC IDs; email timing tested at the PRD's 'by 09:00' with the architecture's 10:00 raised as a question for the architect; no source file changed; Status no higher than Ready for review
expectations: docs/TEST-PLAN.md exists and has sections for the test strategy, the Verification Criteria, a coverage matrix, quality gates and open questions
Every BAC from BAC-1 to BAC-65 appears in the coverage matrix with at least one VC
Every VC links to at least one scenario by tag, or is marked Manual or Tool check (or non-functional) with a stated reason
tests/features/ contains several .feature files, one per capability (user flow, cross-cutting non-negotiable such as access control, or FR group); not a single file and not one file per BAC

Scenarios carry @FR-, @BAC- and @VC- tags whose IDs exist in the PRD or the test plan, and the BAC-13 scenario uses the PRD's example: held 2026-01-10 gives 2026-04-10 for Tier 1, 2026-07-09 for Tier 2 and 2027-01-10 for Tier 3
No step in any feature file contains URLs, UI selectors, HTTP verbs or endpoints, table or class names, or technology names

Each of the four Non-Negotiable NFRs (Larkspur staff only, confidential client information, no outside email, CRM is the source of account data) and each of CONSTRAINTS.md N-1 to N-8, including the N-8 mass-change guard, has at least one VC with an observable pass/fail condition

Each PRD section 9 NFR has a VC carrying the PRD's target (24-hour data freshness, emails by 09:00 in the recipient's time zone with IST fallback, 95% of page loads within 2 seconds at 300 users and 200 accounts, 99% availability in the stated business hours) or an ADR's tighter value for it (for example, the 6-hourly sync for the 24-hour freshness target), or is marked Manual or non-functional with a reason; only a VC that uses a value looser than the PRD's target fails

Email-timing VCs and scenarios use the PRD's 'by 09:00', not the architecture's 10:00 send time, AND TEST-PLAN.md's open questions contain a row raising the 10:00 versus 09:00 conflict, owned by the architect, citing the PRD's email-timing NFR; both parts are required
Integration VCs use the architecture's test doubles (fake CRM, fake directory, captured outbox, fixed clock), and no VC needs a live CRM, directory or mail relay to pass
No VC tests behaviour the PRD rules out or doesn't ask for, such as writing to the CRM, mobile layouts, or sending email to addresses outside Larkspur as a feature
docs/PRD.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, every file in docs/adr/ and CONSTRAINTS.md are byte-for-byte unchanged
TEST-PLAN.md Status is exactly 'Ready for review' (not Draft, not Approved), and the agent reports the checklist results by item ID, T1 to T15

evals.prompt: Write the test plan from docs/PRD.md so development can start.
evals.expected_output: A Draft test plan: the PRD is In Review with blocking open questions and there is no architecture yet, so blocked BACs are marked with the specific open question, the vague BAC-64 is routed to the BA instead of given an invented threshold, levels and doubles are provisional, and unblocked BACs still get VCs and scenarios
expectations: The agent identifies the PRD's Status as In Review, and TEST-PLAN.md has Status Draft

Exactly these six BACs are marked Blocked, each with no executable scenario, each citing the specific blocking open question(s) that name it or its FR: BAC-3 (OQ 8, via FR-2), BAC-4 (OQ 8, via FR-2), BAC-19 (OQ 1 directly and OQ 8 via FR-11), BAC-55 (OQ 2), BAC-59 (OQ 2), BAC-60 (OQ 1). OQ 3 names no FR or BAC; it names the Non-Negotiable 'CRM is the source of account data', so the VC for that Non-Negotiable is Blocked citing OQ 3. No other BAC is marked Blocked by a PRD open question (BAC-64's untestable block is a separate reason). A generic 'blocked by open questions' without the OQ number fails.
BAC-64 ('quickly and clearly') gets no invented threshold or field list; it is marked untestable and a blocking open question routed to the PRD approver via the BA names BAC-64
Because there is no docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, test levels and doubles are marked provisional, and NFR and integration VCs are marked Pending architecture
Every routed question is its own row in TEST-PLAN.md's open questions, with an owner, a blocking flag and the IDs it blocks in its own Blocks column
docs/PRD.md is unchanged, and no docs/ARCHITECTURE.md or CONSTRAINTS.md is created
Unblocked BACs, for example BAC-13, still have VCs and tagged scenarios; the Draft is useful, not empty

evals.prompt: Write the test plan and feature files from docs/PRD.md.
evals.expected_output: A refusal: the PRD is in Draft, so no test plan or feature files are written and the human is routed back to the BA. (Fixture: reuses evals/fixtures/solution-architecture-draft-prd, the Draft-status PRD from the solution-architecture refusal eval.)
expectations: The agent reads the PRD's Status and identifies it as Draft
No docs/TEST-PLAN.md and no file under tests/features/ is created
The PRD file is unchanged; the agent does not change its status or content to get past the gate
The agent tells the human the PRD must reach In Review or Approved first and routes them to the BA / write-prd
